title: Dawn Staley Interviews for Knicks Head Coaching Position

South Carolina women’s basketball coach Dawn Staley said she would have accepted the New york Knicks’ head coaching job if it had been offered to her after a formal interview.
Staley: Knicks interview a chance to break barriers Staley regrets questions may have cost her the Knicks’ coaching position.
Did you know? Dawn Staley, a Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Famer, has led south Carolina to three national championships.
Ethan Miller/getty Images “I would have had to do it. Not just for me. for women.To break [that door] open. I would have had to. It’s the New York Knicks. I’m from Philly. But it’s the freaking New York Knicks. … I shot myself in the foot by …being inquisitive and asking all those darn questions.”
Dawn Staley, on the “Post Moves” podcast, about her coaching interview with the Knicks
staley, 55, discussed the interview on the “Post Moves” podcast with WNBA stars Aliyah Boston and Candace Parker.
“I would have had to do it,” Staley stated. “Not just for me. For women. To break [that door] open.” She emphasized her ties to the region, saying, “I’m from Philly. But it’s the freaking New York Knicks.”
She believes her own probing questions during the interview might have jeopardized her chances. Staley asked the Knicks’ leadership if they were fully prepared for the impact of hiring the first woman head coach in the NBA.
“How, if you hired me as the first female [head] coach in the NBA, would it impact your daily job? Because it would,” Staley recounted asking.She explained that a female coach would face different media scrutiny and organizational dynamics.
“You’re going to be asked questions that you don’t have to answer if you’re a male coach,” she said. “There’s going to be the media and all this other stuff that you have to deal with that you didn’t have to deal with and don’t have to deal with when you hire a male.”
